record_notes.DCP-LETT-2175F: November29 [1857] five-block complete Darwin ALS, five footnotes read. F suffix does not imply fragment; later complete catalogue facsimile superseded excerpt. Lubbock report heard yesterday, observer initially friend of Bate; asks species/specimen, insertion duration/depth/position, recipient cirri/valves/vigour, water and named authority. Requests forwarding to friend, not proof of completed forwarding here. November30/December1 cover postmarks differ from composition. Extant Bishop-to-Bate December3 identified by apparatus/CSV2179, now separate recovery candidate; no exact Darwin receipt or new direct incoming-to-Darwin target inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1835: Morris March1,1856, eight blocks, six notes, annotations and bibliography read. Helix identification attributed to Wood; Melaniopsis identity doubtful. Little species-duration evidence distinguished from strong persistence of freshwater genera. Grays stratigraphic order unresolved. Recalled geological-paper reversal lacks reference, lookup promised; later Murchison revision in apparatus not Morris present knowledge. No missing Darwin inquiry or promised later letter reconstructed. Trailing Darwin address separate from signature.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1941A: Norman August17 [1856], two blocks and three notes read; body taken from Frank Nicholas transcript, underlying ALS metadata/private repository not claim of viewed original. Copy completed well; additional3d per1000 of15000 gives3s9d, plus9d pamphlets totals4s6d;19s6d+4s6d=24s=£1 4s. Preserve nondecimal currency and distinguish future1s/1000 rate. Date backed by account entry, no proof recipient delivery. Manuscript identification and later Hooker reading are apparatus. Raw markup inspected, no MathML.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1872: May10 [1856], three blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Vaux introduces reported Oldfield resemblance of Assyrian drawings and Tibetan dogs; Darwin questions closeness from possibly poor drawings and asks other Nepal breeds/domesticated birds. Body ear/chop observations are drawing comparison, not own live-animal fieldwork. Later Variation reports Oldfield judged dogs different, not an already received answer. Cover London address consistent with leave, no invented current Nepal residence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2036: January4 [1856], two blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Supplied year tied to November20,1855 extant1782F, not catalogue-ID1857 chronology. Quatrefages recipient inferred as intermediary. Missing kind note promises to seek Flourens information; not receipt of information. Journal sent through Williams/Norgate, no delivery proof. Variation project not expected for years; current varieties kept, not complete eventual dataset.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2139: September8 [1856], three blocks, three notes and bibliography read. George home September5–8 and Crystal Palace meeting establish supplied year. Class standing better than anticipated, well-grounded subjects attributed to Reed tuition; not blanket top rank. Asks no acknowledgement; P3 substantive post-closing request. No written incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1929: Richardson July17,1856, seven blocks, five notes, annotations and bibliography read. Personal comparative salmon/pike species judgment distinguished from disputed American taxonomy, untested Pacific salmon comparisons, doubtful Bering limit, approximate40th parallel and reported Malta/Aral cases. Trout/Galaxias external resemblance not identity; freshwater versus marine southern overlap, genus versus species and anadromy distinct. P5 authorial addition inserted by edition according to footnote, not modern annotation. Hurried answer to missing questions; later manuscript parallels may derive from earlier1836/1845 works.2072 named Richardson comparison alone does not uniquely identify this letter as source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2142: Schlagintweit September25,1857, four blocks, four notes, annotation and bibliography read. Acknowledges missing Darwin September20 note; claims Chooboo fertility to7th generation from collected observations/information, not described controlled pedigree experiment. Castrated animals observed and unpacking/further details still future. Journal speech/report source earlier than later1861–66 expedition publications. Footnotes refer to CD note above but actual letter div contains only body, brief annotation, footnotes and bibliography: separate note text unavailable. Annotation displays18 while note4 says17 portfolio, preserve discrepancy without rewriting.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2167: Smith November10,1857, three blocks, five notes, annotations, bibliography and actual figure read. Missing Darwin earlier request may be oral or written. Bates letter quoted inside Smith body reports both worker forms from several nests; preserve nested Bates attribution, not Darwin voice. Smith earlier figured large worker as species; now sends relative-proportion tracings and suggests future oral response, no actual reply. Actual figure shows larger left major worker with broad oval disc head and smaller right minor with small squarish head, labels Cryptocerus discocephalus and I-shaped marks without numeric units; no inferred measured scale. Later attachment to species-book chapter not exact letter receipt date. Trailing Chas Darwin Esqre is address.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1841: March11 [1856], one-block copy, three notes and bibliography read. Formal third-person courtesy is Darwin-authored voice, not editorial synopsis. Thanks Spencer gift; reports name entered reading list about fortnight earlier, not read book. Apparatus says no such entry found in surviving list, so retain discrepancy. Light annotations establish no exact reading day. Date supplied from publication, not target hallucinated first-person rewrite.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1853: April13 [1856], three blocks, five notes, excluded Private heading and bibliography read. Thanks for Entomologist Weekly Intelligencer issue, discusses Stainton remarks and three-year-old Royal Medal rule change. Personal agreement not disclosure of confidential Council discussion. Darwin/Hooker/Westwood listed under changed rule; avoids evaluating own award. Newsletter editorial described/partly quoted in apparatus, not complete incoming text. Earlier1767 Annual/list matter different publication. Private marker historical header, not current instruction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2001: November26 [1856], four blocks, six notes and bibliography read. John Thompson recipient conjectured from later payment, not certain solelyXML. Promised rabbit death/carcase, secretary request already sent, potential Vivian bird deaths/assistance future; no specimen delivered here. Comb-related skull claim not securely restricted to already examined Crève-Coeur individual as summary implies. Full P4 postal-address instructions require final body/address span separation. January1857 payment and later publications not current receipt evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2378: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Darwin-to-Mueller December 8 with year supplied, two blocks, full notes/bibliography read. Uses William and Joseph Hooker names as introduction, asks whether British/northern European perennials can live and set seed in hot southern Australia, controlling competing native plants and possibly watering; southern European success only presupposed. Naturalized British plants partly answer question, enumeration requested, not received. Later missing Mueller reply cited in manuscript is not surviving input or already known here. Specific Hooker December 6 recommendation and introduction permission demonstrably used by December 8, before December 9 direct answer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-366F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Fresh prior context: Monday evening July24,1837 inferred from July25 postmark. Seven blocks, eight footnotes and bibliography. Asks northern forest extent, species, frozen subsoil and nearshore ice extent/temperature to test megafauna/vegetation and burial hypotheses. Prior Richardson house conversation remembered, incomplete reference lookup. Treasury petition remains pending, laterAugustgrant not yet known; Journal writing slow. P7 follows address/signature but is substantive authorial continuation. Restored damaged characters preserved, no missing answer synthesized.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-370F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Fresh prior context: Friday assignedAugust11,1837 from expected visit near15th and grant chronology. Seven blocks, eight footnotes and bibliography. Unofficial intelligence this morning of£1000order, laterAugust16 official interview distinct. Requests half-hour meeting, not actual appointment. Thanks unlocated long climate account, still dissatisfied with mammoth ice-burial explanation; later proof-stage resolution not backdated. Richardson last-letter travel plan and climate account may be related but no preserved source proves one or separate inputs.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1267F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November4, supplied1851 ALS explicitly incomplete. Two surviving blocks, four footnotes and bibliography; unreadable word and two lines retained as gaps. Cirripedes safely received by writing, return in few weeks promised. Wants Assistance Bay location for Sutherland range data, absent from gazetteer; later modern location and1854 published ranges not yet current answer. Original partial source cannot be completed from December outgoing or apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1466H: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December30, supplied1851 ALS. Four blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Tomorrow handoff to carrier, Thursday railway booking, Friday/Saturday hoped receipt are future stages, not actual delivery. Under Tuesday dating these imply December31 handoff, January1 rail, January2/3 expected arrival; apparatus says Thursday carrier travel, which may differ from handing parcel to carrier. Do not flatten all to Thursday dispatch or prove receipt. Requested enclosed names absent from online body. All specimens British species, high-latitude ranges valuable. Richardson expedition account reading underway lately, no full completion date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1471: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. January 10, supplied 1853 ALS. Four blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Bate new residence and continuing work seen in Annals publication, not necessarily received personal note. Requests Verruca on noncalcareous and limestone substrata for comparison; existing few Devonshire specimens do not settle solvent hypothesis. Later results and 1854 published acknowledgment remain future. Metamorphosis follow-up question not an incoming response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1511: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 1, supplied 1853 ALS. Three blocks, six footnotes, bibliography and actual MathML. Slate and Old Red Sandstone specimens received, observed no boring; still seeks limestone specimens. Bate many-specimen report and carbonic-acid suggestion conveyed through missing communication. Darwin believes solvent for Verruca, mechanical friction in other boring cirripedes; these are stage-specific views. Requests independent reinspection of complemental males, not completed confirmation. Caustic potash instruction has MathML numerator 1 denominator 4, one quarter hour, not fourteen hours; historical procedure not current advice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1521: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 7, supplied 1853 ALS. Five blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Missing Bate note reports Alcippe discovery; citation promised, not current publication. Limestone search still unfulfilled, specimens in next two or three months could help. Copies already made from two Bate drawings for early larval stages, attribution promised; permission assumed without fresh request. Earlier permission to refer to paper does not automatically establish specific copied-figure permission. Later printed plate references remain outcome evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1528: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. August 30, supplied 1853 ALS. Three blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Latest specimen inspected and Darwin considers it sufficient with previous facts to support calcareous-only action. His evidential judgment is not modern verification. Carbonic-acid reference now requested because previous Bate letter mislaid; does not prove original printed paper read. Lubbock oral report of related crustacean research remembered imperfectly; journal identity only imagined and later Quatrefages identification probable. Published 1854 distinction against Bate respiratory-current mechanism cannot be backdated into current request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1767: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October20, supplied1855 one-page ALS. Three blocks and two footnotes. Declines name insertion because no longer collects/works on an insect order, confirms missing slip correct. Apparatus addresses list of British entomologists with addresses; summary masthead unsupported. Later1856 omission separate from current request. Statement does not preclude all later insect-related correspondence or change taxonomic interests beyond its stated scope.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1782F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November20, supplied1855 complete four-page ALS, not fragment. Three blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Quatrefages Souvenirs gift read every word, with apparatus October30 completion distinct. Earlier kind note absent. Flourens third-generation hybrid sterility claim read without experimental details, seeks replication/cross-to-pure versus inter-hybrid distinction, not endorsing universal result. Horse pamphlet ordered but unavailable for sale, asks alternate venue/copy. Journal offered conditional on English reading, later January4 letter corrected from1858? to1856 records sending; future probe, no current delivery. Address Farnborough exception does not override literary dating.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2072: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April5, supplied1857, six retained blocks, all twelve notes and bibliography read. Seeks authoritative Dana opinion to test Richardson comparison of temperate versus polar fish distributions against Crustacea, acknowledges scant southern data. Purbeck mammals personally seen at Falconer, whereas prospective Lyell supplement not yet received. Tentative Plagyoulax spelling and mammalian identification are current account, not silently modernized. Lizard importance and Prestwich reaction separate from new mammal classification by Owen; one-character objection qualified despite authority. Gray correspondence broadly acknowledged without a uniquely identified current letter.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Root viewed actual JPEG. Two ant-worker outlines labeled major and minor, larger left with broad oval disc head, smaller right with small squarish head. Caption Cryptocerus discocephalus; I-shaped marks and worker symbols, no numeric dimensions or units. Body describes relative proportions; no scale value inferred.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
